locator: §5.2, 'If there is no more robust understanding of truth conditions than can be secured by minimalism about truth conditions, it will be difficult for the quasi-realist non-cognitivist to make the distinctive negative semantic claim'
interpretation: The collapse argument's minimalist premise, held by the deflationists who use it 'to argue that there is no room for non-cognitivism'. The entry states it only as the antecedent of a conditional, so the claim attributes it to those defenders, not to the entry. Read as: whatever is minimally truth-apt is also robustly truth-apt, since no more robust truth-aptness exists. Only the direction from minimal to robust is formalized. Minimalist non-cognitivists regroup by distinguishing minimal from robust belief and representation (Blackburn 2006; Sinclair 2006; McDonald 2012, as reported in the same section); the entry does not say in so many words that they reject this premise. Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the position the entry reports, not a thesis of the entry's author. No primary text is pinnable (in copyright, no immutable open text).
